units.source_statement: Evaluate the original finite Itô row at a common bounded stopping time capped by the evaluation time. The dyadic squared-increment sum of this stopped row converges in L¹ to the original square energy accumulated up to that stop, with integrable signed error at every level.
assumptions_inventory: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is progressive and product-space square integrable. One [0,T]-valued stopping time τ is shared by all coordinates and satisfies 0 ≤ τ(ω) ≤ T at every sample point.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Identify the stopped row at every grid endpoint
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Use the fixed-time stopping theorem at all endpoints of one finite grid. This identifies the actual stopped row with the completed row of closed stopped integrands almost surely.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Identify the stopped energy
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Squaring the stopped integrand preserves its indicator. Integrate the original coefficient squared on the closed interval ending at τ.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Apply the progressive-row theorem
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Stopping preserves progressive L². Replace the row values and energy at each level by their identified counterparts and use the already proved L¹ limit.

units.boundary: The grid is deterministic. The single common stop is random and is applied to every row evaluation.
units.proof_topology: Identify the actual common stopped row at each endpoint of a finite deterministic grid; square the closed stopped-integrand indicator; transfer the progressive-row L1 quadratic-variation theorem.
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: The stopping time is [0,T]-valued, not necessarily finite-range. Fixed-time almost-sure endpoint identities suffice separately for each finite grid; the energy identity must use the closed cutoff with Lebesgue time. No natural-math defect found.

units.source_statement: The prefix integral of an integrable real time density has finite variation on the closed horizon.
assumptions_inventory: The horizon T is nonnegative. The real density b is integrable against nonnegative time measure restricted to [0,T].

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Control one increment
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: A prefix increment is the integral of b over one time cell. Its absolute value is bounded by the integral of |b| over the same cell.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Telescope the bound
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Sum the bounds on any finite nondecreasing list of times in the horizon. The absolute-density prefixes telescope, and the final prefix is finite.

units.boundary: The Lean conclusion records bounded variation. The proof establishes the displayed quantitative bound, including T=0.
units.proof_topology: Control an ordered prefix increment by the corresponding absolute-density integral; telescope over arbitrary finite nondecreasing horizon partitions.
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: The displayed increment now explicitly requires 0<=s<=t<=T. The half-open prefix and closed integral endpoints require nonatomic time. The theorem concludes bounded variation while the displayed quantitative bound is promised inside its proof, including T=0.

units.source_statement: For distinct coordinates of the same Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted sum of their simultaneous increment products vanishes in mean square on dyadic grids.
assumptions_inventory: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration.
Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint.
One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Read the mean-square conclusion of the mixed-increment theorem
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The preceding theorem proves both square integrability at each dyadic level and the asserted vanishing second moment. Select its second conclusion; no extra moment or independence assumption is introduced.

units.boundary: Mean-square control of the literal mixed increment sum for the specified grid weights.
units.proof_topology: Select the mean-square conclusion from the preceding mixed-increment theorem.
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: This is explicitly a consequence: no independent proof or stronger claim is made. The producer must have identical weights, coordinates, Brownian driver and uniform moment bound, and must actually prove square integrability.

units.source_statement: If f is C² at every point of the segment from x to x+v and its Hessian differs there from D²f(x) in operator norm by at most ε, then the Taylor residual has norm at most ε‖v‖².
assumptions_inventory: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
For every t∈[0,1], f is C² at x+tv and ‖D²f(x+tv)−D²f(x)‖≤ε. The constant ε is real; these assumptions imply ε≥0.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Differentiate along the segment
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: After subtracting the first derivative and the Hessian at x, the derivative of the first-order error is exactly the Hessian variation applied twice to v.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Bound the first-order error
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The operator-norm bound controls D′. Since D(0)=0, the mean-value inequality on the unit interval bounds D by the same constant.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Apply the mean-value inequality a second time
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The residual along the segment has derivative D and starts at zero. Evaluating its bound at t=1 gives the conclusion.

units.boundary: The constant is an upper bound; no optimal factor of one half is asserted.
units.proof_topology: Differentiate the first-derivative error along the segment; apply the Hessian operator norm estimate and mean-value inequality; differentiate the Taylor residual and apply mean value again.
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: The hypotheses imply epsilon>=0 at t=0. The argument needs normed-space mean-value inequalities, not completeness or finite dimension. No natural-math defect found; no optimal one-half constant claimed.
dependency_edges: norm mean-value inequality on a segment

units.source_statement: For the dyadic grids on [0,T], suppose all predictable weights have second moments bounded by one constant C, uniformly over levels and cells. Their compensated weighted square-increment sums tend to zero in mean square.
assumptions_inventory: B is a real Brownian motion with the given filtration and measure. The horizon T is any nonnegative real.
At every level n and cell i, the real weight is strongly measurable at time iT/2ⁿ and is in L². A real C satisfies E[aₙ,ᵢ²]≤C for every n,i.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Apply the exact finite-grid identity
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Bound each diagonal weight moment by C and sum the equal cell lengths.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Let the mesh tend to zero
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The upper bound tends to zero and the integrand is nonnegative, so the squeeze theorem gives the limit.

units.boundary: This is mean-square convergence of a centered error, not an almost-sure convergence assertion. It includes T=0.
units.proof_topology: Use the exact finite-grid second moment identity; replace weight moments by a uniform C; sum squared dyadic cell lengths; squeeze by 2*C*T*(T/2^n).
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: A nonempty dyadic grid and the second-moment bound imply C>=0. T=0 must remain permitted. Gaussian increment moments and predictable orthogonality belong to the finite-grid dependency, not to extra assumptions on weights.

units.source_statement: On any compact pseudometric time space, take finite grids whose neighboring time distances vanish uniformly. If the sums of squared state increments converge in measure to a real-valued random variable Q, then the sums of second-order Taylor residuals converge in measure to zero.
assumptions_inventory: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.

The time space is compact and pseudometric. Each grid has Nₙ+1 points, and for every δ>0, eventually all neighboring time distances are less than δ. Q:Ω→ℝ is a finite real-valued function. No ordering of the time space is required.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Establish measurability of the residual sums
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The restrictions of f, Df and D²f to K are continuous. Hence the residual as a function of two K-valued endpoints is continuous, and the finite random sums are measurable.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Extract a pathwise convergent energy subsequence
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: From any subsequence, convergence in measure provides a further subsequence on which the square-increment sum converges almost everywhere. On each such continuous path it is eventually bounded by C=|Q|+1.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Combine small increments with the uniform Taylor estimate
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Uniform continuity of each path turns the time-mesh condition into small state increments. Apply the compact uniform residual estimate with tolerance ε/(2C). The residual sum is then bounded by ε/2. The subsequence characterization yields convergence in measure.

units.boundary: Convergence of square-increment sums is an explicit input to this reusable lemma; the downstream Itô theorem derives it for its actual process. No rate or almost-sure limit for the full sequence is asserted.
units.proof_topology: Prove continuity of the two-endpoint residual kernel on K times K and measurable finite sums; extract an almost-sure energy subsubsequence from each subsequence; use path uniform continuity and a compact uniform Taylor estimate; return to convergence in measure.
units.bridge_obligations_and_natural_math_chec: Only neighboring distances are needed; no time ordering or coverage assumption. Q is finite real and C=abs(Q)+1 is positive. C2 at K supplies local ambient neighborhoods for uniform Taylor control even without convex K. The whole sequence is claimed only to converge in measure.
dependency_edges: almost-sure extraction from convergence in measure
